run016_c02_exact.classification: continuous engineering-objective proxies, not customer limits, CAD, payload mass, or supplier quotations
run016_c02_exact.candidate: C02-A6F1 with minimum physical channel-camera envelopes

largest_optic_and_external_aperture.next_largest_basis: SWIR doublet mechanical clear diameter; failed optical attempt retained only as a packaging lower-bound witness

characteristic_lengths.classification: sequential optical coordinates; dichroic branch folding and cells are not modeled

bounding_box.relationship_to_run014: consistent with the lower edge of the 64-157 L C02 architecture hypothesis
bounding_box.limitations: not a CAD envelope; excludes wall thickness, cells, baffles, electronics, thermal hardware, dichroic branch separation, focus travel and gimbal clearance

major_optic_mass_proxy.assumption: solid annular primary and solid secondary; thickness/diameter 0.10; density 2.2 g/cm3, matching Run 014 proxy convention
major_optic_mass_proxy.limitations: not payload mass; actual sag, central-hole reinforcement, lightweighting, material, facesheet, ribs, mounts and qualification can dominate

large_optics.interpretation: one large common primary; secondary; two SWIR and two EO trial camera elements; dichroic clear aperture must exceed the approximately 52 mm SWIR beam after tilt allowance

shared: front baffle and primary-secondary metering structure

structural_and_gimbal_consequences: single approximately 314 mm front aperture sets gimbal frontal area
approximately 645 mm straight sequential extent would create a long inertia arm unless channel paths are folded
annular f/1 primary and secondary spider require print-through, vibration and line-of-sight jitter analysis
shared fore-structure removes the duplicated telescope-datum/parallax burden of C01 but concentrates both channels on one primary-secondary alignment

optical_performance.common_front_best_curved_focus: near matched obscured-pupil limit at EO and SWIR corner
optical_performance.flat_detector_burden: approximately 60-63 mm focal-surface radius requires strong channel field flattening

manufacturability_and_cost.assessment: f/1 is feasible in principle but this diameter, sag, hole and support geometry require custom fabrication and metrology; no quote or production yield exists
manufacturability_and_cost.backend_assessment: two spherical elements per channel are insufficient; at least one more field-flattening/achromatizing degree of freedom is likely, increasing optic count, coating count, barrel length and tolerance burden

run016_c02_exact.pareto_decision: optically credible common-LOS lane, but not accepted over C01/C03/C04 because primary mass proxy, straight length, obscuration and backend complexity remain material; retain conditionally and establish the C01 practical comparator next
